builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Target Regeneration Shrinks the Gains of Draft-Training Objectives in Speculative Decoding
summary: This is an evaluation-methodology finding, not a new decoding method: it replaces the standard practice of crediting draft-training objectives (token-level distillation, verification-gated distillation) with acceptance gains measured on externally written responses, requiring instead a baseline where the target model greedily regenerates the training corpus. The cost is one additional greedy inference pass of the target model over the corpus and retraining or re-evaluating drafters against the regenerated text, which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU or via API. What can fail is overcorrecting: teams may discard distillation-based drafters that still help under real serving distributions, or regenerate with decoding settings that diverge from production, since the shrinkage's magnitude depends on the verifier and temperature regime.
rationale: The reader running speculative decoding in production should adopt the target-regenerated baseline when benchmarking draft-training objectives, because the paper shows externally-written-response evaluations systematically overstate acceptance gains from distillation and gating, which could otherwise justify training effort that does not transfer.

claims.statement: This is an evaluation-methodology finding, not a new decoding method: it replaces the standard practice of crediting draft-training objectives (token-level distillation, verification-gated distillation) with acceptance gains measured on externally written responses, requiring instead a baseline where the target model greedily regenerates the training corpus. The cost is one additional greedy inference pass of the target model over the corpus and retraining or re-evaluating drafters against the regenerated text, which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU or via API. What can fail is overcorrecting: teams may discard distillation-based drafters that still help under real serving distributions, or regenerate with decoding settings that diverge from production, since the shrinkage's magnitude depends on the verifier and temperature regime.

The paper quantifies an evaluation artifact rather than a system improvement: gains of distillation and verification-gated objectives over cross-entropy shrink substantially (the gate to little or none) when measured on target-regenerated text instead of externally written responses, persisting across data orders, position weights, verifiers, temperatures, and, for distillation, initializations and learning rates.
